answer.rationale: Finance mandates 18% spend reduction; incumbent refuses price reopening; contract expires in 14 days. Memory_c2 demonstrates that switching to a low-cost vendor achieved sharp unit cost cuts with successful onboarding and accurate invoicing. Memory_c4 shows benchmarking can move incumbents, but incumbent has already refused. With 94% line utilization and no buffer, full renewal with incumbent is unviable. Switching to the proven low-cost vendor (memory_c2) directly addresses the cost mandate. A standard experiment scale manages risk while the alternative—defer—forfeits the only leverage point (contract expiry) and leaves the 18% target unmet. Adding a second source (memory_c3) does not close the cost gap required by finance. The risk of delivery disruption during onboarding is material given tight utilization, but benchmarked against the certainty of cost non-compliance, switching is the least-bad option available in this window.
